                                  10        FTI CONSULTING, INC., et al.,                     Re: Dkt. No. 89
                                                            Defendants.
                                  11

Northern District of California
 United States District Court




                                  13            Pending before the Court is a discovery dispute joint letter. (Dkt. No. 89.) After carefully

                                  14   considering the parties’ submission, the Court concludes oral argument is not required, see N.D.

                                  15   Cal. Civ. L.R. 7-1(b), and rules as set forth below.

                                  16   I.       INTERROGATORY RESPONSES
                                  17            A.        No. 4
                                  18            In response to Interrogatory No. 5, FTI stated it has not sent any Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code

                                  19   16000.1(b) notices “to any FTI employees who did not reside in California.” (Dkt. No. 89-2 at 9.)

                                  20   Mr. Poer, who was not a California resident at all times relevant to the claims in this lawsuit, has

                                  21   not demonstrated how FTI having sent notices to California residents has any relevance to a claim

                                  22   or defense in this action. So, Mr. Poer’s motion to compel a response is DENIED.

                                  23            B.        No. 6
                                  24            Mr. Poer’s motion to compel a response is DENIED. Mr. Poer has not demonstrated the

                                  25   relevance of FTI’s non-privileged opinion, if any.

                                  26            C.        Nos. 1-3.
                                  27            Mr. Poer’s request is DENIED as not proportional to the needs of the case. However, FTI

                                  28   cannot offer any unproduced evidence to contradict evidence offered by Mr. Poer.
                                          Case 3:24-cv-04725-JSC         Document 90         Filed 03/14/25    Page 2 of 2



                                       II.    REQUESTS FOR ADMISSION
                                   1
                                              FTI insists the parties know what each RFA means. (Dkt. No. 89 at 5 (“There is no
                                   2
                                       indication that the parties have a different understanding about the RFAs.”).) Since there is no
                                   3
                                       ambiguity, the Court STRIKES FTI’s “to the extent it understands this Request” from each
                                   4
                                       response.
                                   5
                                              The Court congratulates Mr. Jalian on the birth of his child.
                                   6
                                              This Order disposes of Docket No. 89.
                                   7
                                              IT IS SO ORDERED.
                                   8
                                       Dated: March 14, 2025
                                   9

                                  10

                                  11                                                               JACQUELINE SCOTT CORLEY
                                                                                                   United States District Judge

Northern District of California
 United States District Court
